title: SET THE TABLE
goal: Activate prior knowledge about friendship and teamwork, build curiosity about the mystery, and introduce key mission vocabulary.
outcomes: Share prior knowledge and questions about friendship and teamwork.
Explain selected mission words using examples.
Make a prediction about the upcoming mystery.
prep_note: KWLS sheets in the Core Workbook; pencils; School Song sheet or vocabulary reference; selected Vocabulary Cards or Party Planner. Prepare only the activities you choose. Resource links pending verification.
focus: Listen for meaningful connections between vocabulary, friendship, and teamwork.
assessment: During the closing share, check whether students can explain a word or support an idea. Clarify unfamiliar vocabulary as needed.

rows.text: Introduce “Team Switch Detected!” using the current Set the Table lesson slides once approved.
How might you feel if a teammate switched teams without telling you?
Core Workbook KWLS: complete K with prior ideas and W with a question. Save L and S for Part 5.
What are you most curious to find out?
A — School Song OR B — Mission Vocabulary.
A — School Song: Play “Triple C”. Students collect 10 words or phrases on their School Song sheet; share and clarify selected words.
What do these words tell us about the school's values?

B — Mission Vocabulary: Introduce adaptability, communication, emotional regulation, and collaboration through definitions and brief examples. Partners explain one word in their own words; look for the ideas in Chapter 1.
A — Vocabulary Cards OR B — Party Planner.
A — Vocabulary Cards: Give each group a selected set of word cards. Sort into “Know,” “Think We Know,” and “New”; check unfamiliar meanings.
A — Choose two words and explain what they might look like when a team's plan changes.
B — Party Planner: Give students the Party Planner sheet. Partners choose six words, sort them, and explain which three they would invite onto a strong team.
Revisit Friendship Mystery #1 using the approved lesson slide once verified.
Share one new word, idea, or prediction.
